finding: fp16 significantly reduces measured inference memory, but not by exactly 50%.
evidence: fp16 reduced peak allocated memory by 47.22% for distilgpt2 and 47.48% for gpt2.
interpretation: Total runtime memory contains parameters plus activations, KV cache, buffers, framework overhead, and allocator effects.

finding: Parameter-memory reduction is not equal to total runtime-memory reduction.
evidence: Theoretical fp16 parameter reduction is 50%, but measured runtime reduction averaged 47.35%.
interpretation: Memory estimators must separate parameter and non-parameter components.

finding: Quantization metadata reduces ideal int8/int4 savings.
evidence: At group size 128, int8 effective reduction became 74.22% instead of 75%, and int4 became 86.72% instead of 87.5%.
interpretation: Scale and zero-point metadata must be included for realistic analytical quantization estimation.

finding: int4 is more sensitive to metadata overhead than int8.
evidence: At group size 128, metadata overhead was 3.125% for int8 and 6.25% for int4.
interpretation: Lower-bit formats have smaller raw weight memory, so metadata becomes proportionally larger.

finding: The QuantizationMemoryEstimator makes quantization logic reusable.
interpretation: Quantization estimation is now part of the project architecture, not only notebook analysis.

finding: The total-memory approximation is more realistic than parameter-only estimation.
evidence: It decomposes measured fp32 runtime memory into parameter and non-parameter memory.
interpretation: This gives a better estimate of practical memory savings under dtype/quantization changes.

finding: int8 and int4 results are still analytical, not measured runtime profiling.
evidence: No real int8/int4 quantized model was loaded or profiled.
interpretation: The project should not overclaim quantized runtime results.
